claude_fable_5.1_high/001:
Since the API gives only the piece placement, my policy contains a complete self‑written chess engine:

1. **Board model**: 10×12 mailbox board, Zobrist hashing, incremental material + piece‑square‑table score, incremental non‑pawn material counts for phase detection.
2. **Move generation**: full pseudo‑legal generation for all pieces (promotions to all four pieces). Castling and en‑passant are deliberately *not* generated because castling rights / last move are unknown from the state – returning one of these could be illegal and cause disqualification. Every move is verified legal by make/unmake + king‑attack test, so only legal moves are ever returned.
3. **Search**: iterative deepening negamax alpha‑beta with a transposition table, null‑move pruning, check extensions, killer moves + history heuristic + MVV‑LVA ordering, and a quiescence search (captures/promotions; full evasion search when in check, delta pruning). Time is controlled by a deadline (~0.5 s) with a safe fallback: the best move from the last completed iteration (or a fully searched improvement in the partial iteration) is always available.
4. **Evaluation**: material + PST (simplified‑eval tables), endgame king table when material is low, insufficient‑material draw detection, and a mop‑up term (drive the lone king to the edge, bring our king closer) so that won endings are converted. A small penalty discourages repeating positions already reached earlier in the game.
claude_fable_5.1_high/002:
Since the API only gives the piece placement, the policy contains its own complete chess move generator (pseudo‑legal generation + king‑safety filtering, promotions included). Castling and en passant are deliberately never played because the state does not include castling rights / last move, so they can't be verified as legal — every returned move is guaranteed legal. If, in the astronomically rare case, no ordinary legal move exists, an en‑passant capture is returned as the only possible remaining move.

On top of the generator sits a fast pure‑Python engine:
- Negamax alpha‑beta with iterative deepening under a strict time budget (~0.6 s, checked every 512 nodes; falls back to the best fully‑searched root move if interrupted).
- Quiescence search on captures/promotions with delta pruning, so material is never dropped to simple tactics.
- Transposition table with Zobrist hashing (incrementally updated), killer moves, history heuristic, MVV‑LVA ordering, check extensions, null‑move pruning (disabled in low‑material endgames) and late‑move reductions for extra depth.
- Evaluation = material + piece‑square tables (incrementally maintained), tapered king tables (middlegame vs. endgame), and a "mop‑up" term to drive the enemy king to the edge in won endgames (so K+Q/K+R vs K gets converted).
- A cross‑call repetition memory: positions seen earlier in the game score as draws in search, so the engine avoids threefold repetition when ahead and seeks it when behind.
- Everything is wrapped in fallbacks so a legal move string is always returned.
claude_fable_5.1_high/003:
Since only `pieces` and `to_play` are given, I build a full chess engine from scratch:

- **Board**: 10x12 mailbox with integer piece codes (positive = white, negative = black), incremental Zobrist hashing, incremental tapered (middlegame/endgame) material + piece-square-table evaluation, plus a mop-up term (drive the enemy king to the edge, bring our king closer) for won endgames and an insufficient-material draw check.
- **Move generation**: pseudo-legal generation followed by an explicit "is my king attacked" legality test after every move, so checkmate and stalemate are scored correctly. Castling and en passant are never generated (their legality can't be inferred from the state), so every returned move is guaranteed legal.
- **Search**: iterative deepening negamax alpha-beta with a transposition table, PVS, null-move pruning, futility pruning, late move reductions, check extensions, killer/history heuristics and MVV-LVA ordering, and a quiescence search with delta pruning. Repetition avoidance uses both the search path and a memory of positions previously handed to the policy.
- **Time control**: a hard deadline (~0.7 s) enforced via node-count time checks; the best move from the last fully-searched root move is returned. Everything is wrapped in fallbacks so a legal move is always returned.
claude_fable_5.1_high/004:
Since only the piece placement is given (no castling rights, en‑passant square or move history), the policy contains its own full move generator and search engine:

1. **Board & move generation** – 64‑square mailbox, pseudo‑legal generation for all pieces (all promotions to queen/knight, double pawn pushes). Castling and en‑passant are deliberately never generated because their legality cannot be verified from the state alone (returning an illegal move would disqualify us). Legality is enforced by a king‑attack test after each move (skipped cheaply when the mover cannot possibly expose the king).
2. **Search** – iterative‑deepening negamax alpha‑beta with quiescence search (captures/promotions, check evasions with mate detection), transposition table, null‑move pruning, check extensions, late‑move reductions, killer/history move ordering and MVV‑LVA. Time is checked every 512 nodes and the search is aborted at ~0.55 s; the best move from the last (or partially completed) iteration is used.
3. **Evaluation** – incremental material + piece‑square tables (with separate middle‑/end‑game king tables), insufficient‑material draws, and a mop‑up term (drive the bare enemy king to the edge, bring our king close) so that K+Q/K+R endings get converted.
4. **Repetition avoidance** – a module‑level memory of positions seen in the current game (reset when the piece count changes); repeating a known position scores as a draw, so the engine makes progress when winning and seeks repetition when losing.
5. **Safety** – the returned move is re‑verified on a freshly built board; any exception falls back to a verified legal move.
claude_fable_5.1_high/005:
Since the `policy` function only receives the piece map and side to move (no legal-move list), the policy contains its own full chess implementation:

- **Board & move generation**: 10×12 mailbox board with pseudo-legal generation for all pieces, then legality filtering by make/unmake + king-attack test. Castling and en-passant are never generated (their legality depends on unknown history, and an illegal move would mean disqualification); promotions always to queen.
- **Evaluation**: incrementally-updated tapered (middlegame/endgame) material + piece-square tables, insufficient-material draw detection, and a "mop-up" term (drive enemy king to the edge, approach with our king) so won endgames are actually converted.
- **Search**: iterative-deepening negamax alpha-beta with quiescence search (MVV-LVA, delta pruning), transposition table with Zobrist hashing, killer moves, history heuristic, check extensions and null-move pruning. A hard time budget (~0.62 s) is enforced through a timeout exception; the best move from the last fully completed iteration is returned.
- **Repetition avoidance**: positions seen in earlier calls of the game are remembered (module-level set) and scored as draws in search so the engine makes progress when ahead.
- **Safety**: legal moves are computed before searching so a legal fallback always exists; the whole thing is wrapped in exception handling.
